question.text: Under Section 135(5) of the Companies Act 2013 and its Rules, a company liable to CSR is required to spend at least:

answer.text: 1% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 2 financial years
2% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years; projects of INR 1 crore or more mandatorily require impact assessment
2.5% of net profit of the current financial year only
5% of turnover of the immediately preceding financial year

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 135(5) of the Companies Act 2013 requires a CSR-liable company to spend at least 2% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding three financial years on CSR activities. The CSR Rules separately require an independent impact assessment for CSR projects with an outlay of INR 1 crore or more where the company also has an average CSR obligation of INR 10 crore or more. The Trap: Option A understates the rate (1%) and uses a 2-year average. Option C uses an incorrect rate (2.5%) and the wrong base year. Option D uses a turnover base — CSR spend is profit-based, not turnover-based. Note: The cited SIA workbook supports the CSR impact-assessment trigger for companies with average CSR obligation of INR 10 crore or more and CSR projects of INR 1 crore or more, but does not on the pages checked specifically state the Section 135(5) 2%-of-three-year-average-net-profit spend rule. The spend-rate framing above reflects the Companies Act 2013 itself rather than a workbook-page citation.
